items.title: Lula tired of Putin waging war and Trump "saying he has the biggest ship" during campaign rally
items.author: Associated Press
items.content:
<article>Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said Saturday he was “tired of seeing Putin wage war” and hearing U.S. President Donald Trump boast about having the biggest ships and rockets, as he campaigned in a historic working-class neighborhood in western Rio de Janeiro ahead of October’s elections. items.title: Mexican ranchers prepare to resume livestock sales to US under tight controls over screwworm risk
items.author: Associated Press
items.content:
<article>Cattle ranchers in Mexico’s northern state of Sonora are preparing to resume exports to the United States after more than a year of disruptions caused by the spread of the New World screwworm, but they say the initial flow of cattle will be too small to quickly clear a backlog.

items.title: Pope visit micro-state of San Marino and speaks of liberty and the value of life
items.author: Associated Press
items.content:
<article>San Marino, a nation of about 35,000 people completely surrounded by the Italian state, traces its origins to the fourth century. It is governed by a 60-member parliament that elects two captains regent every six months to serve jointly as heads of state, a power-sharing arrangement designed to prevent the concentration of authority. Using the micro state as an example, Leo argued that small political communities can offer lessons in public service and social cohesion at a time of growing division and distrust.

items.title: Obesity drugs show early promise against PMOS
items.author: Associated Press
items.content: <article>A small but growing body of research shows that GLP-1 drugs often used to treat obesity may also work for the hormonal disorder known as PMOS. They're believed to help not only by promoting weight loss but also by improving insulin resistance, hormone balance and ovulation.</article>
